proof_audit.reasoning: For each b, minimize the separate intercept to get ybar−xbar prime b. Substitution leaves the M objective, whose Gram quadratic form is the sum of squared transformed linear combinations. Full within rank gives uniqueness; constant columns are annihilated. A particular unit effect retains its fixed-T average disturbance.
proof_audit.boundary: Exact algebra; no causal or consistency conclusion without separate assumptions.

proof_audit.topic: Mean restrictions and fixed-T within asymptotics
proof_audit.reasoning: Strict E[u_t|X,c]=0 centers X prime M u. With iid whole vectors, fixed p,T, finite fourth moments of X,u and positive within Q, H and g are square integrable. LLNs and continuous inversion prove consistency before the unit-score CLT gives Q inverse B Q inverse. The common effect is removed exactly and needs no fourth moment in this proof.
proof_audit.boundary: Sequential or contemporaneous exogeneity alone need not center the transformed score; increasing T and heterogeneous slopes require new analysis.

proof_audit.reasoning: The exact relation ghat=g−H delta yields the two-term norm bound. Finite squared H and g make both bounding averages O_p(1); consistency makes the bound o_p(1). The true-score outer-product law requires only the established square score moment. Studentization additionally requires a positive limiting contrast variance.
proof_audit.boundary: Covariance of beta-hat is Vhat/N; no exact t or few-unit coverage theorem.

proof_audit.reasoning: P and M are orthogonal projections. Omega has eigenvalues sigma_u² and sigma_u²+T sigma_a² on the two subspaces. Inversion and A=M+(1−theta)P give A prime A=sigma_u² Omega inverse with sigma_u²>0 and sigma_a²>=0.
proof_audit.boundary: A known positive working weight may target a biased projection; mean conditions and conditional covariance efficiency conditions are distinct. Infinity is a limit of weights, not an invertible covariance.

proof_audit.reasoning: Reparameterize dated slope b and mean slope d as (b,b+d). Because each weighted within deviation sums to zero under a common within-unit weight, the objective splits into full-rank within and between objectives. Their separate minimizers determine the exact sample equality and all coefficients.
proof_audit.boundary: Only balanced same-sample linear common-weight identity proved. Structural mean coefficients require E[c|X]=alpha+xbar prime pi and strict idiosyncratic conditional mean zero; mean-projection orthogonality alone is insufficient. Population structural interpretation also requires the explicitly stated finite augmented moments and positive population Gram.

proof_audit.reasoning: Initial y0=0, effect zero and independent fair e1,e2 give regressor (0,e1). Each within Gram is 1/2 and numerator yields rho−1+e1e2. Averaging iid units proves exact mean rho−1, variance1/N and that probability limit.
proof_audit.boundary: This is a specific bounded two-transition law, not a stationary Nickell formula.

proof_audit.reasoning: With independent third innovation, z=y1 is orthogonal to e3−e2. The relevance expectation is rho−1 and squared score mean is2. Exact ratio expansion and iid unit CLT give root-N variance2/(rho−1)² at each fixed rho unequal1. Under the general stated sequential conditional mean, iterated expectation centers instruments measurable two dates back.
proof_audit.boundary: At rho1 this moment is flat in proposed coefficient; no claim of whole-data nonidentification. Finite denominator can vanish; near-boundary uniformity, system GMM, large moment dimension and serial innovation validity are not inherited.

proof_audit.reasoning: Finite always-observed H and E[R|W,H]=p(H)>=epsilon imply E[R psi/p|W,H]=psi with integrability supplied by bounded inverse probabilities.
proof_audit.boundary: Positivity is not MAR; finite variance separately needs moments. Missing-outcome alternatives show no unrestricted point identification.

proof_audit.reasoning: Write the estimate as sum pi_hat a_hat/b_hat. At positive population denominators its derivatives are (mu_h,1/p_h,−mu_h/p_h). Joint iid finite-dimensional CLT and differentiability give influence mu_H−mu+R(Y−mu_H)/p_H. Orthogonality conditionally on H yields Var(mu_H)+E Var(Y|H)/p_H. Plug-in consistency follows finite-cell laws for count,Y,Y².
proof_audit.boundary: The baseline-frequency fluctuation cannot be omitted. Empty response-cell event is explicitly unavailable; a fixed auxiliary value only supports the asymptotic sequence because its probability is exponentially small.

proof_audit.reasoning: Known-p unnormalized weighting has influence RY/p−mu. Its difference from the fitted-cell influence is mu_H(R/p−1), orthogonal to the latter under MAR. The variance gap E[mu_H²(1−p)/p] is nonnegative for these exact estimators.
proof_audit.boundary: No universal estimated-propensity efficiency theorem or conflation with normalized known-p ratio estimator.

proof_audit.reasoning: Date demeaning leaves (lambda_i−mean lambda)F_t; balanced two-way demeaning leaves (lambda_i−mean lambda)(F_t−mean F). Centered q,s leave the teaching design/error untouched, making beta-hat=2+U and every unit score2U. Full cross-unit covariance gives variance4 for the average score.
proof_audit.boundary: The common-shock law is explicitly separate from the iid-unit theorem. Conditioning changes the target, and zero fitted residual covariance does not restore consistency. No general factor/two-way-cluster theorem.

exercise_solution_audit.exact_prompt: A study follows eight firms for three dates, regresses outcomes on lagged outcomes and chosen investment, adds firm and date effects, discards nonresponding firms, and reports row-iid standard errors. It concludes that investment causes growth because a random-effects comparison test did not reject. Give six distinct objections tied to identification or inference, two feasible redesigns or sensitivity analyses with limited claims, and a concise conclusion the existing design could honestly support.
